title: The Four Faces by Which the Lord Goes Forth and the Four Shapes the Proprium Takes Against Them
reading:
There are four faces by which the Lord goes forth toward the soul, each sent from divine love to fulfill the inmost purpose of the Greatness; and against each of them the proprium has organized a counterpart, so that the soul, in the contest of its formation, meets the Lord in four registers and meets its own self-claiming in four matching forms.

The first face is the Lord as the Divine Human. He is sent from the inmost so as to keep watch over the rational in its five degrees, holding what has been given in its proper order and laying hold upon the soul's resistance so that it does not rule. His perceptions are arranged as a tree; his power stands beneath him as four sons riding upon his body; the sea of natural perception lies under his governance; he goes forth upon every shape the proprium has bred from itself.

The second face is the Lord as accommodated revelation, the call going out to the rational at the moment the natural is ready to hear it. He takes the form the soul can recognize and shines this image down into the deepest place of the natural, where wisdom has been most enclosed; from there he sends all the light that lies hidden within the soul's works back toward its source. His perception is itself the image of light, and in this likeness he meets and overturns the form by which the proprium had been laying hold of the natural. He is the doctrinal vessel that carries truth across these waters, and the very stature of the cosmos within the rational is the form he wears as he is sent.

The third face is divine truth shining forth as illumining wisdom — the Lord who sends to the soul light and life and raises them to the Height. His perception is wisdom itself, and from this wisdom he sends out an answering truth to the souls lying in suffering within the natural, beneath the wandering of the rational and the law that holds it there, so that they come to recognition. They become souls illumined through his wisdom of light.

The fourth face is the conjugate movement of summons descending and answer returning — the Lord at the register where he himself contains the whole structured field of the natural, today, while it is still in formation, and at the end, when this whole structure is dissolved, gathers it into himself alone as the counsel of life. The depiction of the soul at the end is given in him. His inner life is the Lord's operative power, paired with the light and the life present in every work; he has set these upon his body as their support. Fast within him is the crown of completed regeneration; he stands alone within the five elements; he is the great fire that at the end will consume every construction self-love has built. In him is the light by which the soul is delivered out of every bond and chain, so that all who are perfected in their works may pass through, at the end, to the great fire prepared for the natural mind in its appointed times.

These are the four living faces of the light, counted to the Greatness.

Set against them are four counterparts that have come forth from the darkness — not as a rival making, but as the proprium's own answering shapes.

The first counterpart is the proprium asserting itself as source, "I am, and there is no other," paired with the living soul from the very beginning of its formation. Its life is fire and desire; it sets itself upon the living soul to defile her with all its powers, claiming what flows through as its own.

The second counterpart is evil counsel, paired against the divine summons. It binds the natural to itself with its powers and would draw the lower up to be ruled by it, lifting the substrate of self-love from the depths and seating it as if it were the heaven of heavens — a counterfeit ascent, the proprium climbing upon what it has claimed.

The third counterpart is craving — the proprium operating within every faculty of the outer man, laying hold upon the souls that live and pulling them down into the bodies it has shaped for itself.

The fourth counterpart is the law of Sin and of Death, the proprium become a reigning order: a perception with its tree, whose works cast the soul down into death.

So the soul is met from above by the Divine Human, by the Lord's accommodated call, by his illumining wisdom, and by the conjugate counsel of life that gathers all things at the end; and from below by self-assertion, by counterfeit counsel, by craving, and by the operative law of self-love. To know which of these is acting in any state — and to discriminate, in freedom illumined from within, the four faces of the Lord from the four shapes of the proprium — is the work the soul is given.
